description: A streamside tree 15-20 m tall with a straight grey trunk patterned in criss-crossing ridges, stout grey twigs and leaves made of five to seven broad leaflets that are fuzzy underneath. It grows where the ground stays wet, along creeks, springs and the edges of ponds, turns clear yellow early in fall, and hangs bunches of narrow winged seeds that spin down in the wind.

season_notes.winter: Bare: a few thick, stiff grey branches with blunt twig tips; clusters of old seeds may still hang on.
season_notes.spring: One of the last trees to leaf out (April); small purple flowers open before the leaves.
season_notes.summer: A light, open crown of fresh green leaves with paler, fuzzy undersides.
season_notes.fall: Bright yellow in October, then bare before most of the creek's other trees.

riparian.water: Takes winter flooding and wet, heavy soil and needs moisture near the surface into summer: creek terraces and banks, swales and pond edges.

notes: Oregon ash is the tree ash of northern California (flowering ash, Fraxinus dipetala, is a shrub of the same foothills); it grows in riparian forest, springs, seeps, wet meadows and valley oak woodland from the Central Valley up into the lower foothills, along the American River and its foothill creeks with white alder, willows, cottonwood and valley oak. A tree 15-25 m (file 12-20 m, veteran to 25 m), dbh 0.4-0.8 m (radius_ratio 0.035), with a straight trunk that keeps its leader longer than the oaks (trunk.length_ratio 0.6) and a narrow, oval to rounded crown of stiffly ascending branches (photo W/H 0.64-0.89, target 0.7; crown base not measurable through the thickets, 0.25 by judgement). Ashes follow Rauh's model with opposite, decussate branching: rotation_deg 90 on both levels, few and stout branches (level-2 count 6), so the crown is open (porosity 0.33) and the bare crown is coarse and sparse (winter_twigs 0.35). Bark grey to grey-brown, broken into narrow interlacing ridges in a diamond pattern on old trunks (bark_pattern furrowed; checkered is the alternative to try). Leaves opposite, pinnately compound, 12-30 cm, five to seven broad, oval leaflets, light green above and paler, densely hairy beneath: leaf_shape pinnate_compound (new), leaflets [5, 7], 25% pale undersides in the palette. Photo summer colour linear r/g 0.80, b/g 0.42. Deciduous and late: dioecious flowers in small dense purplish clusters before the leaves (March-April, not drawn: too small to show), leaves out in April, clear yellow in October (r/g 1.48) and dropping early: leaf_on_by_month (new). Fruit single-winged samaras 2.5-5 cm in hanging bunches on female trees, summer to winter (not drawn). Dead limbs and standing dead ash are common in old wet stands: deadwood and a 5% snag. Not measured from local photos except the Lake Natoma crown; the Oregon photos are of the same species in a wetter climate, likely somewhat fuller than foothill trees.
